messages:
Olivia M: Heads-up — after the driver 565 rollout to the us-west-2 GPU pool ~12 nodes failed to come back. Pods are CrashLooping or stuck Pending for GPU resources. Seeing DKMS build failures in journal.

InfraBot: Deploy finished: driver-565 rollout -> 88% succeeded, 12 failures reported. See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/driver-rollouts/565

Olivia M: sample journal snippet from one node:
```
Jul 12 08:23:41 host kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and required key missing
Jul 12 08:23:42 host dkms: ERROR: Failed to build module nvidia-565 for kernel 5.15.0-1066-azure (x86_64)
Jul 12 08:23:42 host dkms: make: *** No rule to make target '/lib/modules/5.15.0-1066-azure/build', needed by 'modules'.  Stop.
```

Raj P: can we cordon/drain the remaining nodes in the canary group and reimage? If headers are missing reimaging with our standard image that includes linux-headers should fix.

Leo K: quick root cause guess: some machines are running an "optimized" kernel package (azure-custom) where linux-headers were stripped to save space. Driver 565's DKMS build requires the full headers tree. The previous driver (535) used prebuilt module we packaged in the image so it didn't trigger a build.

Leo K: verified on one failed host: `uname -r` -> `5.15.0-1066-generic`, but `/lib/modules/5.15.0-1066-generic/build` is a broken symlink to nowhere. Attempting `apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)` returns 404.

Olivia M: also seeing cloud-init loops on a couple nodes where initramfs got regenerated after dkms failed, which changed module dir names and made kubelet unhappy: nodes flapping between NotReady and Ready.

Raj P: mitigation plan (short):
- cordon + drain failed nodes
- rollback driver package on new nodes to 535 via image or apt pin if possible
- reimage nodes that can't build DKMS
- stop further rollout until we add a headers check to the pipeline

Mike S: rolling back will force some jobs to move to on-demand / spot fallback and we're already seeing a 3x GPU cost delta for affected jobs. need to cap preemptible autoscale while we heal.

sre-oncall: immediate commands I ran on one node:
```bash
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo dkms remove -m nvidia -v 565 --all || true
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
sudo update-initramfs -u
sudo reboot
```
That brought a node back to Ready in ~4m.

Leo K: long term: add this to rollout gating: verify `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build` exists and that `linux-headers-$(uname -r)` is available in our apt mirrors. If not, fail the canary automatically and don't push.

Olivia M: also noticed some distributed training jobs emitted NCCL warnings: `NCCL WARN No NVIDIA driver found, aborting` which made controllers redeploy CPU-only tasks. That increased cost and experiment timeouts. We should mark GPU nodes as "tainted:needs-driver-fix" during the incident so schedulers don't assign heavy jobs.

Mike S: agreed on taint; I've temporarily limited batch job concurrency in the GPU namespace to reduce cost exposure.

Raj P: I'll open a ticket with images team to ensure that our gpu images include headers or have a fallback package. Also filing infra-issue: #INFRA-2147 (link: https://issues.internal/redwood/INFRA-2147)

InfraBot: Incident created: INFRA-2147 — driver 565 rollout caused DKMS/kernel-header mismatch in us-west-2 GPU pool. Priority: P1.

Olivia M: action items captured:
- [Raj] coordinate image rebuild with headers included
- [Leo] add headers presence check to rollout gating + canary script
- [sre-oncall] rollback nodes and reimage in affected pool, cordon/taint until healthy
- [Mike] keep cost throttles and monitor GPU spend dashboard

Olivia M: I'll sit on a quick sync in 15 to confirm progress. :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: quick note — if we want to avoid DKMS builds entirely for future driver bumps we can prebuild and bake modules into certified images and skip DKMS on boot. More upfront work but faster recovery.

Olivia M: agreed. For now we stop the rollout, rollback canary, and schedule a careful re-roll after images + gating. Thanks everyone.
